title: South Africa at the World Cup
description: Hosts of 2010 and the birthplace of the vuvuzela — how well do you know Bafana Bafana's World Cup story?

questions.q: South Africa hosted the 2010 World Cup — a historic milestone for African football. What was special about this?
options: It was the first World Cup in the southern hemisphere
It was the first World Cup held on the African continent
It was the first World Cup decided by goal line technology
It was the largest World Cup ever by attendances
questions.explain: The 2010 World Cup was the first to be held on the African continent, marking a landmark moment for African football. South Africa beat other African bids to become the host nation.

questions.q: Who scored South Africa's famous opening goal of the 2010 World Cup against Mexico in the tournament's second match?
questions.explain: Siphiwe Tshabalala curled a stunning left-footed shot into the top corner against Mexico — the first goal of the 2010 World Cup and one of the most celebrated in South African football history. The match ended 1–1.

questions.q: South Africa became the first host nation to be eliminated in the group stage. What result denied them a round of 16 spot?
options: They drew with Mexico and lost to Uruguay, but beat France — not enough on goal difference
They were disqualified for fielding an ineligible player
questions.explain: South Africa drew 1–1 with Mexico, lost 3–0 to Uruguay and beat a disgraced France team 2–1. Despite the France win, they went out on goal difference — the first host nation eliminated in the group stage.

questions.q: What instrument, closely associated with the 2010 World Cup, drove fans and television viewers around the world either wild or mad?
questions.explain: The vuvuzela — a long plastic horn — became the defining sound of the 2010 World Cup, producing a constant loud buzz. FIFA considered banning it but ultimately allowed it, dividing global opinion.

questions.q: South Africa made their World Cup debut in 1998. Who managed them to a respectable showing in France?
questions.explain: Clive Barker guided South Africa to their first World Cup in France 1998, where they drew with Spain and Saudi Arabia but were eliminated in the group stage. South Africa were one of the most popular teams with neutral fans.

questions.q: What is South Africa's national team nickname, translated to mean 'Boys of the Boys' in Zulu?
questions.explain: Bafana Bafana — meaning 'The Boys' or 'Boys of the Boys' in Zulu — is the beloved nickname of the South African national football team. The women's team is known as Banyana Banyana.

questions.q: Which South African striker is the national team's all-time top scorer and starred in the 1998 and 2002 World Cups?
questions.explain: Benni McCarthy is South Africa's all-time top scorer, netting 31 international goals. He also had a prolific club career in Europe, winning the Champions League with Porto under José Mourinho in 2004.

questions.q: South Africa qualified for the 2026 World Cup — their first since 2010. Through which confederation?
questions.explain: South Africa qualify through CAF — the Confederation of African Football. With 9 CAF places at the 2026 World Cup, it was a competitive qualifying process against Africa's strongest nations.

questions.q: In 2010, South Africa's quarter-final hopes were ended by Uruguay. What was the score?
questions.explain: Uruguay beat South Africa 3–0 in the group stage, effectively ending the host nation's qualification hopes. Uruguay's Luís Suárez, Álvaro Pereira and Diego Forlán all scored.

questions.q: The Johannesburg stadium used as the centrepiece of the 2010 World Cup was newly built. What is it called?
questions.explain: FNB Stadium — known as Soccer City and designed to resemble a traditional African calabash — hosted both the opening match and the 2010 World Cup final (Spain vs Netherlands). It remains Africa's largest football stadium.
